findings.claim: getDataWithMetadata takes the object length from the GetObject response, which with the default multipart client is part 1's Content-Length, not the object's size.
findings.failure_mode: If merged as-is, on S3 storage with the default storage.s3.multipartEnabled=true every complex obs over 8 MiB reports length 8388608 instead of its real size. legacyui's ComplexObsServlet sends ComplexData.getLength() as Content-Length, so the download ends at 8 MiB with no error. CI can't catch it because S3Mock ignores partNumber.
findings.evidence: Read SDK 2.32.13 sources (the version `mvn dependency:list` resolves): DownloadObjectHelper.downloadObject splits into partNumber GETs, and SplittingTransformer forwards only the first part's onResponse upstream. Throwaway test against a local HTTP stub that honours partNumber the way AWS documents it: multipart=true gives getDataWithMetadata.length=8388608 with bytesRead=20971520 and getMetadata (HEAD)=20971520; control multipart=false gives 20971520. Throwaway test against the S3Mock 4.5.0 container: a partNumber=1 GET returns the full 20971520 with no Content-Range, so S3StorageServiceIT can't see the bug. With the suggested getObjectLength applied, the stub run gives 20971520 for both modes and spotless:apply leaves it unchanged. javap of legacyui-omod 3.0.0-SNAPSHOT ComplexObsServlet: ComplexData.getLength() goes into setHeader("Content-Length").

findings.claim: read() falls back to the legacy location only on NoSuchFileException, so a legacy file whose percent-encoded name exceeds the 255-byte name limit fails with 'File name too long' and is never read from the legacy location.
findings.failure_mode: If merged as-is, legacy complex obs saved before 2.8 with titles of 36+ Cyrillic or 24+ Amharic characters stop loading once storage/<obs dir> exists (that is, after the site saves any new complex obs). AbstractHandler throws UncheckedIOException, TextHandler throws APIException, and ImageHandler silently returns no image. Master reads all of them.
findings.evidence: Throwaway BaseContextSensitiveTest drove AbstractHandler.getObs on legacy files appdata/obs/<title>_<uuid>.txt with storage/obs present. At the head: 35 Cyrillic letters OK, 36 Cyrillic FAIL with FileSystemException 'File name too long', 24 Amharic FAIL, 80 ASCII OK. Without storage/obs all four pass, because ENOENT on the parent comes first. Master worktree (891b80745) with the same test: all four OK. With the proposed FileSystemException fallback applied: all four OK, and LocalStorageServiceTest plus the AbstractHandler/Text/Image/BinaryStream/BinaryData/Media handler tests (69 tests) pass. spotless swaps the NoSuchFileException import for FileSystemException. Pre-2.8 naming read at df94143ec:api/.../AbstractHandler.java:65.

findings.claim: The only call-count test covers AbstractHandler.getObs, which all five bundled handlers override, so TRUNK-6682's no-reintroduction criterion is not met for any handler that actually runs.
findings.failure_mode: If merged as-is, TRUNK-6682 closes with its third acceptance criterion unmet: a redundant exists probe or separate getMetadata re-added to any bundled handler passes CI, which is the regression the ticket asked tests to prevent.
findings.evidence: Mutation: added storageService.exists(key) to BinaryStreamHandler and replaced dwm.metadata() with storageService.getMetadata(key) in TextHandler. LocalStorageServiceTest, AbstractHandlerTest and the six handler tests stayed green (68 tests). Control: the same getMetadata mutation in AbstractHandler.getObs turned getObs_shouldNotIssueRedundantStorageCallsForLocalStorage red (expected 0 but was 1). grep shows getObs overridden in BinaryStream/Image/BinaryData/Media/TextHandler. The handler fields storageService/adminService are package-private in org.openmrs.obs.handler, so tests in org.openmrs.obs need ReflectionTestUtils.

findings.claim: exists() no longer checks that the current-location path stays inside the storage dir, so for absolute keys it reports whether an arbitrary file exists where master threw IllegalArgumentException.
findings.evidence: Throwaway test, head: exists("/etc/passwd")=true and exists("/etc/nonexistent-zz")=false. Master worktree: both throw IllegalArgumentException. getData refuses both on head and master. The draft's narrower guard still left exists("/etc/nonexistent-zz")=false. With the full suggested body applied, both throw IllegalArgumentException as on master, and LocalStorageServiceTest, AbstractHandlerTest and the BinaryStream/Image/Text handler tests (60 tests) pass. spotless leaves it unchanged.

findings.claim: The null obs-dir guard fixes a pre-existing NPE on master that is unrelated to TRUNK-6682's I/O counts.
findings.evidence: Copied the PR's getObs_shouldNotThrowWhenTheObsDirGlobalPropertyHasNoValue into a master worktree: it fails with NullPointerException ('this.pattern' is null) at key.replaceFirst(getObsDir(), ""). Master's TRUNK-6472 block runs regardless of whether img is null (read in master ImageHandler.getObs).
findings.body: Could this guard and `getObs_shouldNotThrowWhenTheObsDirGlobalPropertyHasNoValue` go in their own ticket? Master throws the same NPE here for a bare-extension title whenever the obs dir property is unset, image present or not, so it's a separate fix from the I/O counts, and keeping it out leaves less to verify here. Nothing breaks with it in.

findings.claim: S3StorageService.getData duplicates getDataWithMetadata's GetObject call and 404 translation.
findings.evidence: Read S3StorageService.java:129-156. Applied the delegation: S3StorageServiceIT (S3Mock via Docker) passes 28/28 and spotless leaves it unchanged. Control: getData returning an empty stream turns 6 of the 28 red.
findings.body:
This can just delegate to `getDataWithMetadata`, which repeats the same GetObject call and 404 translation (the kind of duplication ibacher flagged in `LocalStorageService`, [comment](https://github.com/openmrs/openmrs-core/pull/6535#discussion_r3990739410)), since the GET already carries the headers:

```suggestion
		return getDataWithMetadata(key).data();
```

findings.claim: Reply in the existing dkayiwa thread (in_reply_to 4070873940): at this head new-layout reads meet the one-probe criterion, but legacy-layout reads still make three existence probes, so whether the ticket stays open for legacy obs is still unanswered.
findings.evidence: Throwaway test subclassing LocalStorageService.fileExists to count probes, driving AbstractHandler.getObs at the head. New layout: 1 probe. Legacy layout (appdata/obs/old_abc.txt): 3 probes [storage encoded=false, appdata/old_abc.txt=false, appdata/obs/old_abc.txt=true], plus a failed stat at storage/obs before the legacy probe. The thread's earlier '5 on this branch' figure predates the read() rewrite.
findings.body: At this head a new-layout read is down to one probe, so that half is met. A legacy-layout read still makes three (`exists` misses both locations, then `read` stats the current location before probing the legacy one). Does TRUNK-6682 accept that for legacy obs, or stay open for it?

verdict: Not ready to merge: on S3 with the default multipart client, complex obs over 8 MiB now report a part-sized length that truncates downloads, and legacy obs with long non-ASCII titles stop loading on local storage.
what_i_swept: Gathered the PR body, TRUNK-6682 (including its acceptance criteria and the backport label) and the full review conversation. Diff stat matches (17 files, +692/-69; the two-dot diff differs only by drift). Read every changed main file in full at the head. Step 2: the read-first/fall-back-on-miss shape in LocalStorageService and the default interface method address ibacher's earlier objections (backport/return change, duplication, metadata-before-data ordering), so the approach is not reopened. Verified each draft by execution: an SDK source read plus an HTTP stub and the S3Mock container for D1; a legacy long-name probe on head and on a master worktree, with and without the fix, for D2; handler mutations with an AbstractHandler positive control for D3; an exists() probe on head and master, plus two candidate fixes, for D4; the PR's own unset-obs-dir test run on master for D5; S3StorageServiceIT with the delegation, plus a broken-getData control, for D6. Outward trace: legacyui ComplexObsServlet (Content-Length consumer), S3 getMetadata versus GET metadata fields, injectMissingMetadata semantics, purgeData/getPath precedence, parseDataKey's exists probe and per-layout probe counts, absolute obs-dir keys, and exception-behaviour changes in the Text/BinaryData/BinaryStream/Media/Image handlers compared with master. Pass 2 (outward) produced F7 and the D4 fix correction. Pass 3 re-swept the handlers and storage services and found nothing new.
could_not_verify: D1 was not run against real AWS S3 (needs access). The part-sized Content-Length comes from the SDK 2.32.13 sources plus a local stub that emulates AWS's documented partNumber GET behaviour (206, part-size Content-Length, Content-Range bytes a-b/total, x-amz-mp-parts-count). S3Mock 4.5.0 does not implement partNumber.

The end-to-end truncation in a servlet container was not run (no server allowed). It rests on legacyui's ComplexObsServlet setting Content-Length from ComplexData.getLength() (confirmed by javap of legacyui-omod 3.0.0-SNAPSHOT) and on Servlet-spec response-closing semantics.
The legacyui source link in D1 was dropped because its commit could not be checked offline. The class is named instead.
D2 was reproduced on macOS APFS (255-byte name limit). Linux ext4 has the same 255-byte NAME_MAX, but it was not run there.
notes: D2 only reproduces once the current-layout obs directory (storage/<obs dir>) exists. Without it the lookup fails with ENOENT on the parent, which is NoSuchFileException, and the fallback works, so a fresh test app-data directory hides the bug. The draft D4 suggestion was replaced: guarding only the current-location probe still let exists() return false for non-existent outside paths, while master threw. The posted suggestion adds assertKeyInStorageDir before return false and was tested. The D1 body drops the unverifiable legacyui GitHub link and the Tomcat-specific claim. The D2 body links the pre-2.8 naming at df94143ec, which is in this clone, instead of an unverifiable 2.7 commit. F7 is a reply in the user's own earlier thread and should go in_reply_to 4070873940, not as a new top-level comment. The @since sub-point from the earlier thread is partly addressed (3.0.0); the backport versions can't be known before merge, so I'm staying silent on it. Working copy restored; git status --porcelain is clean.
